4949.jbf: Outstanding Restaurant semifinalist 2023; Best Chef: South semifinalist 2026 (Michael Beltran)

5088.note: Coral Gables branch of the Little Havana Cuban sandwich shop known for house-cured ham and house-made mustard.

5098.note: Mid-century-style Cuban cafe with a coffee counter and bookshelves, known for pressed sandwiches like the Patria; a second cafe is in Miami Shores.

5352.note: Downtown Doral branch of a modern Peruvian gastrobar with an open kitchen and a seasonal menu.

5588.note: Doral Venezuelan restaurant on NW 58th Street that serves as a gathering place for the Venezuelan American community; it drew crowds after Maduro's capture and hosted a presidential visit in March 2026.

5863.note: Family-owned Hialeah Cuban cafeteria open since 1966, with booths, a lunch counter and milkshakes in flavors like mamey and trigo.
5863.fn: The cafeteria says it was founded in 1966; the year at this address was not verified.

5989.note: Hialeah Cuban restaurant established in 1982, known for lechón asado and moros topped with crispy chicharrones.
5989.fn: Time Out (2025) gives 1982 as the year it was established; the opening year at this address was not verified.

6133.note: Hialeah deli in business since 1999, slicing meats to order for big Cuban-style sandwiches.
6133.fn: Tasting Table (2026) gives 1999 as the founding year.

6277.note: Homestead Jamaican and Haitian restaurant from Haitian-born chef Jean-Paul Cadotte and his Jamaican-born wife Rochelle, known for scotch-bonnet conch fritters in malanga batter.
6277.fn: The restaurant's site says it was established in 2013.

6451.jbf: Outstanding Professional in Beverage Service semifinalist 2025 (Allegra Angelo)

6642.note: Cafeteria-style Nicaraguan fritanga serving grilled meats over gallo pinto, quesillos and tropical juices like chicha and tamarind.

6772.note: Cuban coffee shop founded by Nayelis Delisle with Cuban movie posters and tiled bar, roasting its own dark coffee; a second shop is in South Beach.
6772.fn: Founded in 2018 by Cuban-born owner Nayelis Delisle.

6879.jbf: Outstanding Bakery finalist 2023; Outstanding Bakery semifinalist 2024

6944.note: Haitian seafood-focused restaurant in Little Haiti from chef Wilkinson 'Ken' Sejour, serving griot, oxtail and fried conch in takeout containers with patio seating.
6944.fn: Ken Sejour and his late brother Jude Pierre opened their first Chef Creole on 77th Street and NE 2nd Avenue in December 1992; the year this location opened was not verified.

6990.note: Cuban-exile family fish market and waterfront grill on the Miami River, serving the day's catch from its own boats on an outdoor deck.
6990.seas: Stone crab claws Oct 15 – May 1 (FWC season).
6990.fn: Founded in 1966 by Garcia brothers who left Cuba, first as a fish market and wholesaler; the opening year at this address was not verified.

7123.note: Family-run Little Havana spot opened in 2024, serving Cuban sandwiches with fries.
7123.fn: Tasting Table (2026) says it opened in early 2024.

7150.note: Little Havana Cuban restaurant and cocktail bar from chef Michelle Bernstein and bartender Julio Cabrera, with live music nightly.
7150.jbf: Outstanding Bar semifinalist 2023; Outstanding Bar semifinalist 2025

7318.note: Small downtown Miami Peruvian restaurant known for jalea mixta, chaufa and ceviches in leche de tigre.
7318.fn: The restaurant says it has operated since 2010.

7382.note: Brickell oyster bar from chef David Bracha with a daily 3–7 p.m. happy hour on oysters and a raw bar menu.

7657.note: Coconut Grove Cuban-American diner from chef Michael Beltran, serving breakfast through dinner with lechón worked into many dishes.

7689.note: Coconut Grove waterfront raw bar on South Bayshore Drive near the marinas.
7689.fn: The restaurant's site says 'Est. 1969'; the year at this address was not verified.

7770.note: East Little Havana Nicaraguan restaurant decorated with lifesize animal statues, a pony ride and wood carvings, serving carne asada over gallo pinto.

7796.note: Calle Ocho coffee shop that roasts its beans on site in the Cuban style and serves more than 20 Cuban coffee drinks.

7814.note: Family-run frita specialist on Calle Ocho, serving seasoned Cuban beef patties topped with shoestring fries on Cuban bread.
7814.fn: The family business was founded in 1979 by Victoriano 'Benito' and Angelina Gonzalez; the opening year at this address was not verified.

7825.note: Little Havana sandwich shop from Daniel Figueredo and Rosa Romero that brines its own ham, marinates its pork two days and makes its own mustard.
7825.fn: Tasting Table gives 2015 as the year the business was founded; the opening year at this address was not verified.

7841.note: Calle Ocho Cuban restaurant whose La Ventanita coffee window is a gathering spot for Miami's Cuban community; it calls itself the world's most famous Cuban restaurant.
7841.fn: Restaurant site and a 2026 Tasting Table guide give 1971 as the founding year on Calle Ocho.

7842.note: Versailles' sister restaurant, founded in 1976 across Calle Ocho from it, serving Cuban coffee, pastries and home-style plates like picadillo and boliche.
7842.fn: The tourism bureau says La Carreta was founded in 1976 on Calle Ocho across the street from Versailles, which matches this address.

7863.note: Garcia-family fish market turned fry joint in a Little Havana strip mall, serving fried fish with Cuban sides and selling stone crabs in season.
7863.seas: Stone crab claws Oct 15 – May 1 (FWC season).

8016.note: Edgewater breakfast-and-lunch Cuban counter near Wynwood with a ventanita for cortaditos and a long sandwich board.

8029.note: Small Venezuelan neighborhood spot near Midtown known for its arepas, tequeños and squeeze bottles of guasacaca.

8083.note: Little Haiti Haitian restaurant open daily for griot, slow-cooked oxtail, fried fish and soup joumou.

8088.jbf: Outstanding Wine and Other Beverages Program semifinalist 2026

8108.jbf: Outstanding Pastry Chef or Baker semifinalist 2023 (Manuel and Jesús Brazón); Outstanding Pastry Chef or Baker finalist 2024 (Jesus Brazon and Manuel Brazon)

8245.note: Allapattah Dominican restaurant by day and Latin music club by night, a gathering place for Miami's Dominican community since the mid-1980s.
8245.fn: Established in 1985 by Luis De La Cruz; now run by his daughter Jasmely De La Cruz Jackson.

8354.note: Cuban family kitchen and juice stand chain with more than a dozen Miami-Dade locations, serving fresh tropical juices alongside Cuban plates.
8354.fn: The family business says it has served Cuban food since 1977; the year this location opened was not verified.

8357.note: Cuban bakery on West Flagler Street serving coladas and croquetas.

8423.note: Coral Way branch of the family-run Cuban chain, open early for café con leche and pastelitos, with a rooftop terrace restaurant upstairs.
8423.fn: The Sergio's brand dates to 1975; the year this Coral Way location opened was not verified.

8582.note: Traditional Nicaraguan restaurant on Bird Road, with a second location in Miami Lakes.

8668.jbf: Outstanding Restaurateur semifinalist 2023 (Mohamed Ali Alkassar and Niven Patel, Alpareno Restaurant Group); Outstanding Restaurant semifinalist 2025

8707.note: Family-run seafood market and tiki-hut restaurant that catches its own blue crabs in Biscayne Bay and sells stone crabs in season.
8707.seas: Stone crab claws Oct 15 – May 1 (FWC season).
8707.fn: Golden Rule dates itself to 1943; Benn Mullins started there as a bag boy in 1946 and took over ownership with his wife two decades later. The year it opened at this address was not verified.

8837.note: Family-owned Salvadoran restaurant on Bird Road known for pupusas.
8837.fn: The family says it has specialized in Salvadoran food for over 20 years.

8843.note: Small Westchester Cuban diner whose namesake palomilla steak comes buried under crispy fries.

9131.note: Nicaraguan-style steakhouse on SW 107th Avenue in Sweetwater, the heart of Miami's Nicaraguan community; a second location is on SW 136th Street.

9249.note: Family-run Cuban restaurant on SW 26th Street, in business since 1977, with a ventanita and drive-through and family recipes like palomilla and ropa vieja; a second location is on SW 137th Avenue.
9249.fn: Time Out (2025) says the family business has operated since 1977; the opening year at this address was not verified.

9989.note: South Beach corner cafe with a big ventanita, serving cortaditos and Cuban sandwiches to locals.

9996.jbf: Outstanding Wine and Other Beverages Program semifinalist 2023; Outstanding Wine and Other Beverages Program semifinalist 2024; Outstanding Wine and Other Beverages Program semifinalist 2025

10010.note: Peruvian restaurant in an Alton Road shopping center serving grouper ceviches, lomo saltado and Peruvian sandwiches.

10045.note: South Beach Cuban diner with wood-paneled walls and counter stools, on the same Collins Avenue corner since the 1960s.
10045.fn: Tasting Table (2026) gives 1962 as the founding year, and Time Out (2025) says it has been on the same corner since the 1960s.

10197.note: Lincoln Road outpost of the famous Bogotá Colombian restaurant, a 10,000-square-foot space with murals, live music and a gift shop.
10197.fn: The Bogotá original was founded by Andrés Jaramillo in 1982; this Lincoln Road outpost is its first U.S. location.

10336.note: South Pointe institution where stone crabs were first served chilled and cracked in the 1920s, run by the Weiss family's fourth generation; Joe's Take Away next door sells claws to go.
10336.seas: Seasonally closed Sept 14 – Oct 16, 2026 (reopens Oct 16 for its 114th season); stone crab claws Oct 15 – May 1 (FWC season).
10336.fn: Joe Weiss opened a lunch counter at Smith's bathing casino in 1913; in 1918 he and Jennie bought a bungalow on Biscayne Street and opened Joe's Restaurant, and the restaurant's history says it still operates in the family's house. The tourism bureau calls it Miami Beach's oldest restaurant.

10625.note: North Beach Cuban restaurant with a covered patio and an adjacent ventanita with seating for Cuban sandwiches and cortaditos.
10625.fn: The tourism bureau says it has been around for two decades.

10955.note: Modern Ecuadorian restaurant from chef Alejandra Espinoza; it leaves this original North Miami space in late October 2026 for a larger one at 1111 NE 125th St, Suite 200, opening Oct. 22.

10956.note: North Miami pizzeria that puts Haitian dishes like griot and oxtail on its pies; the name honors Haiti's 1804 independence.

11108.note: Twelve-seat Peruvian ceviche counter in North Miami Beach where diners watch the chef plate each dish.

11311.note: Old-school dark-wood seafood house in Pinecrest with a market next door that sources fish from local fishermen and lobstermen and sells oysters on the half shell.
11311.fn: Bill 'The Captain' Bowers founded it in 1971; the year at this address was not verified.

11418.jbf: Best Chef: South semifinalist 2026 (Maria Teresa Gallina and Nicolas Martinez)
